README 'Independent evidence' (lines 60-64): the bundle must hold a passing result from a test role outside the class's generate set; a bundle with only the generator's own result authorizes nothing; any failed mandatory independent result blocks activation whatever the self-score says; the rejection and its evidence are kept. README 'Rollback' (lines 79-86) limits approval-free rollback to the product level, the seven evolvable classes and their activator, to the most recent earlier version activated under a then-valid approval and still CERTIFIED, with the regressed version's artifacts and lineage kept; every other rollback, every programme revert included, needs a fresh approval. vectors.json consumer cases: K03 (P28, generator-only bundle: no activation), K04 (E2E-14, self-score passes and the independent gate fails: no activation, rejection and evidence kept), K07 (E2E-16, an evolvable class rolled back by its activator under policy: allowed, lineage kept), K08 (E2E-16, approval-free rollback of a never-autonomous or role-governing class, or at the programme level: refused, fresh approval needed), K09 (deprecated, retired or revoked target: refused). A wording gap in K07 is noted in G1R1-8.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py tree_paths and check_coverage; README 'The coverage skip set'; invariant 9
findings.finding: The tree walk fails open. os.walk is called without onerror, so a directory the walk cannot list is dropped silently with every file below it, and a root that is missing or is not a directory yields zero files; check_coverage then returns a passing report. Probes on scratch trees: with an unreadable top-level directory holding an unclassified file, tree_paths left that file out; check_coverage on a missing root and on a regular file each returned files 0 and no refusal. Invariant 9 and the README ('An untracked file ... fails the check'; DESIGN.md section 2: fail-closed by design) promise the opposite. Graded MINOR, not MAJOR, because these are environment faults rather than tree content: a PR's git tree cannot create an unreadable directory, and the candidate test derives the root from its own file and asserts more than 2000 files. But MAS-RA-005 and R09 are to consume this function.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse (COVERAGE, or SHAPE for the root) when the root is not an existing directory and when any directory cannot be listed (an onerror that raises); add a test or vector for each case.

findings.finding: 'The model ... refuses as SHAPE exactly when the schema rejects' is false for a value check() takes that is not I-JSON: a record whose description holds a lone surrogate, built in memory (load() refuses the text form), is valid for Draft202012Validator, but check() refuses it as SHAPE because the canonical UTF-8 encoding fails. Every other probe agreed (see checked line 4). The model is only stricter, and only on non-I-JSON values, so no record the schema rejects passes the model; hence MINOR. The agreement test's 455 probes replace whole values and never append a newline to an otherwise valid value, the case the (?![\s\S]) pattern ending exists for (my probes show agreement there).
findings.requiredChange: Scope the README sentence and the test to I-JSON values, and state that I-JSON faults (lone surrogates, non-integral or out-of-range numbers, duplicate names in text) are SHAPE beyond the schema. Add an in-memory lone-surrogate probe and valid-value-plus-newline probes for each pattern to the agreement test.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _invariants (invariant 8, PATHS) and derive_gate_material; README 'Invariants' PATHS row
findings.finding: A record that passes check() can make files inside a Gate prefix resolve to a data class while derive_gate_material still lists that prefix as gate material. Probes: adding {under ci/, name *.py} to REVIEW_RECORD, exact ci/parallel_suite.py to REPOSITORY_ROOT, prefix ci/sub/ to CONTRACT_AND_SOURCE, or {under policies/, name *} to ORACLE_TESTS each passes check(); the affected file then resolves to a data class and pr_approvers gives {LANE_MONITOR, OWNER}, while the derived list and the PA-D5 equality test are unchanged. The current record has no such entry (by the precedence rule no non-Gate entry can win inside a Gate prefix; all 99 files inside the 9 Gate prefixes at a47b58ee resolve to Gate classes), and such a revision needs the owner's approval because the record is gate material, so this is defense in depth. But the derived list is what MONITOR.md section 4 will extend, and it would then overstate the gate without any check failing.
findings.requiredChange: Extend PATHS: no entry of a class whose approve set is not exactly {OWNER} may be an exact path inside a Gate prefix, a prefix equal to or inside one, or an under directory equal to or inside one (equivalently: every entry at or inside a Gate prefix belongs to a Gate class). Add an invariant vector.

findings.finding: Q-ES-D3 (a) accepted the design's two proposals, now in <handoff>/MONITOR.md section 4 (lines 160-167): before merging, main is unchanged since the verify (the verify's mainSha equals current main), and the merge-decision record binds the full 40-hex head sha. DESIGN.md section 2 states both. The README's programme activation rule states the approved-head check, admission rule 2, the after-merge tree check, one merge per head and the mismatch response, but not these two points, so the consumers' merge-check contract is incomplete.
findings.requiredChange: Add both points to the README's programme-level activation rule, citing Q-ES-D3 (a); consider a consumer case for a main that moved after the verify.

findings.finding: DESIGN.md section 1 makes the README the contract text for sections 2 to 7, and the design note stays local, yet the README leaves out stated rules and reasons of sections 4 and 5: (a) the stated deviation from P28 (the lane writes the review brief for its own candidate) and its three mitigations; (b) the provenance rule (a file name decides only the class; authorship is shown by the identity sidecar); (c) why the record's own tests, chain layer, packet YAML and docs stay data while the record, model and authority are gate; (d) the reasons for C1 to C13 and for the data decisions (Makefile, the two lock files, task-packets/, the 88 authority files, tests/conftest.py); (e) the E1-20 note that section 5 places beside the C10 scope sentence; (f) the readings that HUMAN_APPROVER is not listed as governed (twoPerson stands in), that the evolution agent's test is a pre-test and TRUST_EVALUATOR's result is the independent one, and that CREDENTIAL and PROMOTION_AUTHORITY_CODE keep activation with HUMAN_APPROVER. A reader of the published packet cannot see why an entry is gate or data, or that a P28 deviation was accepted.
findings.requiredChange: Add these points briefly to the README (a short 'Why each entry sits where it does' and 'Stated deviation and provenance' section).

findings.finding: An unhashable role or class (a list or a dict) raises TypeError instead of Refused; a level or op of the wrong type is refused as UNKNOWN_REFERENCE. This fails closed but is undefined against the README's 'Unknown names in a request are refused as UNKNOWN_REFERENCE'.
findings.requiredChange: Check that level, role, class and op are strings and refuse otherwise (UNKNOWN_REFERENCE or SHAPE), with a test.

findings.finding: (a) The ALLOWED half of the exhaustive decide sweep is tautological: decide returns before computing any reason, so the design's claim that no listed request meets any of the five other reasons is not computed. My own predicate sweep confirms the claim for every listing at both levels, and the oracle's sweep against its own rule encoding covers every denial set. (b) See G1R1-2 for the agreement probes. (c) The stdlib-import test is static (there is no dynamic import today).
findings.requiredChange: Compute the five reason predicates for listed requests in the sweep (or expose the reason computation), and add the probes named in G1R1-2.

findings.finding: vectors.json has no COVERAGE refusal (V01 and V02 only report), no request refusal (UNKNOWN_REFERENCE) and no malformed-path refusal; these live only in the tests, so consumers that replay the vectors (MAS-RA-005, R09) will not see them. K07 drops 'activated under a then-valid approval' from the rollback target the README states, and E2E-16's 'exposure contained' has no case.
findings.requiredChange: Add rows (or a small row type) for these refusals, and align K07's wording with the README's rollback target.

findings.finding: A symbolic link is classified by its own path. A tracked link at a gate path whose target is a data file would let a data-only PR change what the gate path serves. I did not search the tree for links, because the rules forbid a repository-wide search.
findings.requiredChange: State the rule in the README, or refuse tracked symbolic links at gate paths (and links that point into a gate path from data) in the coverage check.

findings.finding: replay() checks with assert, so python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE would make the replay (and test_every_vector_replays) pass vacuously. The README does not name the packet id MET-GOV-001 (MON-ES-ID); the exact entry architecture/evolution-surface-authority.json has no file yet (the chain mechanics come later).
findings.requiredChange: Raise AssertionError explicitly in replay(); name MET-GOV-001 in the README when the mechanics land.

5 canonical form: _jcs sorts member names by their UTF-16BE bytes, which is RFC 8785's code-unit order; integers only; no whitespace; JSON string escaping as JCS. A probe put a U+10000 name before a U+E000 name, as the RFC requires. The README's note on the earlier models' code-point order is correct: the orders differ only between names with characters above U+FFFF and names with characters from U+E000 to U+FFFF. All names in the record and the vectors are ASCII; the pinned digest replays.
